content.rationale:
rmovtvkt fixed the four relationship sections and what each lists, and it stopped short of how a listed id's node is presented, so an entry on its own ends in an id a reader cannot follow. The panel is the one place in the viewer where a node is already named exactly — a depends_on entry is the id of a specific recorded node — so it is the right place to let that name be followed: making the reader leave the panel and hunt for the box with that id asks them to re-find by eye what the section has just spelled out, and nothing in the graph's layout puts that box nearby, so the listing would name a node and then withhold it. Activation therefore hangs on the listed id, in the section that already names it, and needs no new surface, list or view.

The outcome is deliberately the selection a box click already makes (ltrnmrsr) rather than a second way of showing a node: two selection paths would give the viewer two notions of which node is selected — the panel's and the canvas's — that can disagree, and the panel would then be describing one node while the canvas emphasises another. Routing activation into that same selection keeps one selected node, one detail render and the emphasis selection already drives (noplrntp), so the panel and the canvas cannot drift apart, and ltrnmrsr's click on a box keeps its meaning because the entry adds a trigger to that selection instead of defining a rival one (zkvxornu makes an evaluation a node too, so an entry naming an evaluation selects it the same way). Naming the entry's id as what decides the selected node follows from the same concern: the depends_on and evaluates edges are two directions of the same relations (mkyoyqvt, mnovnnot) and a section's role is the reason a node is listed, not a different node, so letting the section's direction pick the target would make one id select one node in "depends_on" and another in "dependents".

The keyboard half is not an extra commitment but the same one: selection already has recorded keyboard equivalents (ykvrkysl) and the canvas already has Enter as the keyboard click on a focused element (wzqzwsst), so an entry that only responded to a pointer would be the one selection in the viewer a keyboard reader cannot make, and the panel is precisely where a reader arrives holding a specific named id. Enter is the smallest addition; Space is the other key a focused control is activated with, so both act as the entry's click. Both citations are uses and not restatements: this node's keyboard activation of a listed entry is one of the selection equivalents ykvrkysl requires, and Enter on a focused entry is exactly the Enter-select wzqzwsst records, applied to the entry.

The scope stays at selection because the neighbouring questions are each a different commitment with its own licence: how an entry is drawn belongs to a stylesheet decision, what an id that names no node document does belongs to its own commitment, and opening a document changes behaviour far outside selecting, so this node leaves the entry plain, states nothing about unknown ids, and rules out the open-document and double-click variants instead of half-settling them. Its settled outcome is the selection the entry reaches; what else a viewer does in response to a selection is a separate commitment. Nothing here re-decides what rmovtvkt's four sections hold or what ltrnmrsr's detail shows: the node adds one trigger that lands on the selection those prerequisites already define.
content.content:
Every id listed in one of the detail panel's four relationship sections — "depends_on", "evaluates", "dependents" and "evaluators" (rmovtvkt) — is an activatable entry: activating it selects the node that id names and shows that node's detail, exactly as clicking that node's box on the canvas does (ltrnmrsr).

Activation means either of two equivalent inputs on the listed id: a pointer click, or Enter or Space while that entry has focus. The two do the same thing; neither is a variant, a modifier or a second mode. Because a listed id is activatable, the entry is a control the keyboard can reach and invoke rather than inert text, and focus landing on it is what makes the keyboard input possible.

What activation does is one selection, not a second rendering. The selection moves to the node the entry names — the previously selected node stops being selected — and the panel shows that node's detail as it shows the detail of any selected node (ltrnmrsr, vqwoptmu), including that node's own four relationship sections (rmovtvkt). Activation itself inserts nothing into the section the activated entry sits in and the entry keeps its place in its section's list, so after activation the panel reads exactly as it would have if the named node's box had been clicked. This is an additional trigger for that one select-and-show-detail outcome, not a replacement or an alteration of it: clicking a node's box still selects it and shows its detail exactly as before (ltrnmrsr), and the entry simply reaches the same selection. The entry's id is what decides the selected node: the section says why that node is listed — a prerequisite of the selected node, a node it evaluates, a node that depends on it, or an evaluation that evaluates it — while the id names the node, so an id listed in two sections selects the same node from either, and a section's direction never chooses a different node than its id does. An id is a node id of either kind (zkvxornu): the ids in the "evaluators" section name evaluations and are selected exactly as the ids in the other three sections select decisions.

Activation applies only to listed ids, and it leaves the sections' frames as rmovtvkt fixed them: an empty section offers nothing to activate, because its explicit empty state is that section's text and not a control (rmovtvkt).

Activation's outcome is that one selection, and the node claims nothing further for it: it does not open the named node's document in the editor and adds no double-click variant to the entry, because opening a document belongs to the canvas's double-click (trxzsqpv). An entry's appearance is likewise not settled here — the listed id keeps the plain id look it has today, with no class, no style rule and no hover or focus cue added by this decision, so whether an entry is styled, or given a focus indicator, is left to the stylesheet decisions that own appearance. Nor is anything settled for a listed id that names no node document in the graph: this decision states activation for an id that names a node the panel already has.
